title: Prepaid Dental HMO Plans Member Handbook: Your Primary Care Dentist
content:
# Your primary care dentist — Prepaid Dental HMO Plans

Every person covered under the Prepaid Dental HMO Plans is assigned to a primary care dentist. This chapter states how many times the assignment may be changed, when a change takes effect, which dentists a member may change to, and what happens when the assigned dentist's agreement ends.

## The rule

A member may change primary care dentist up to the plan's number of changes per benefit year times per benefit year; a change requested on or before the plan's change cutoff day of a month takes effect on the first day of the next month, and a later request on the first day of the month after.

The new dentist must hold an active Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement with an open panel; a change is not processed while a multi-visit procedure started by the current dentist is unfinished when the plan holds changes during unfinished treatment.

When the assigned dentist's agreement is ending, Cascade reassigns the member before its termination date and that change does not count toward the limit.

## How changes are counted

The count is of the primary care dentist changes for the person that were requested by the member, within the benefit year that contains the request. The benefit year is the calendar year for an individual enrollment and the plan year for a group enrollment. A reassignment made by Cascade because the assigned dentist's agreement is ending is not a member-requested change and does not count toward the limit.

## Which dentist a member may change to

- **Agreement status.** The company's own provider records decide, read before the change is made: the agreement of the dentist the member is changing to — the Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement identified for the new assignment — must be active.
- **Panel.** That agreement's panel must be open.
- **Unfinished treatment.** When the plan holds changes during unfinished treatment, a change is not processed while a multi-visit procedure started by the current dentist is unfinished.

| New dentist's agreement | Panel | Multi-visit procedure by the current dentist unfinished (plan holds changes) | Change processed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active | Open | No | Not barred by these conditions (the yearly limit still applies) |
| Active | Open | Yes | No |
| Active | Closed | Any | No |
| Not active | Any | Any | No |

## When a change takes effect (hypothetical dates, cutoff day of the 20th)

- Requested 20 March: on or before the cutoff day, so effective 1 April.
- Requested 21 March: after the cutoff day, so effective 1 May.
- Requested 15 December: effective 1 January.

## Questions answered

**Does a reassignment caused by my dentist leaving count as one of my changes?** No. When the assigned dentist's agreement is ending, Cascade reassigns the member before its termination date, and that change does not count toward the limit.

**I have used every change for this benefit year. May I change again?** Not within that benefit year; the limit is per benefit year, counted over the member-requested changes in the benefit year containing the request.

**My crown is half-finished. May I change dentist now?** Not while the crown, started by the current dentist, is unfinished, when the plan holds changes during unfinished treatment.
